note: dw-land is the end of the loop and its description names most of the loop's nouns — decisions, gotchas, the backlog, the change doc — which is exactly why task 1 found it stealing dw-shape's writeup prompt. The positives lean on finishing; the negatives on every neighbouring moment that is not finishing.

positives.prompt: this change is finished — wrap it up and file whatever is worth keeping
am I done here, and what should get promoted into the docs before I forget it
close this out and tidy the change doc away
one last pass over the whole diff, then put the leftovers where they belong

negatives.prompt: I am only halfway through — give me a quick look at what I have so far
negatives.note: The timing boundary from the other side. Mid-build is never dw-land.

negatives.prompt: push it and open the pull request
record the goal and the steps for a feature I have not started yet
negatives.note: Task 1 measured dw-land beating dw-shape on a writeup prompt, so this asserts the fix.
